title: Retinoic Acid Receptor γ Is a Ligand-Activated Gatekeeper to Stem Cell Developmental Progression
content: RARg is expressed during embryogenesis by stem/primitive progenitor cells indicating a role in controlling their development. Support to this view is that a physiological level of 10 nM of the RARg agonist AGN205327 blocked stem/progenitor cell differentiation during zebrafish embryo-genesis, mouse gastruloid development, and adult chondro- and osteogenesis. Similarly, transgene expression of RARg or the use of the RARg agonist CD437 enhanced the generation of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from human and mouse somatic cells. RARg regulates many events that control the behavior of stem/progenitor cells regarding whether they develop to give rise to mature cells. RARg positively regulates the expressions of NOTCH ligands and their receptors, TGFs, and molecules pertaining to cell identity, extracellular matrix communication, and all-trans retinoic acid synthesis and catabolism. The genes that are repressed by RARg include RARg, PPARg, and RXRa. RARg integrates into Wnt/b-catenin and TGFb signaling by acting as a co-factor to the gene coactivator b-catenin and transcription factor Smad3, respectively. Within the cytoplasm, RARg regulates Akt/NF-kB signaling. We consider that ATRA liganded RARg acts as a gatekeeper to stem cell developmental progression during embryogenesis and that this role extends to stem/progenitor cell homeostasis within adult tissues.
